title: priv-eks-lifecycle: declarative management-plane terraform module with preflight and canary health runner
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a reusable, idempotent Terraform module that provisions Redwood's Private EKS management-plane components with automated preflight checks and a lightweight canary health-runner to validate upgrades before promotion. The module should be usable for sandbox, internal, and customer-managed VPCs and integrate with state locking, KMS encryption, and existing provisioning playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Module exposes variables for encryption (KMS key arn), state locking table, and node pool sizing
Module supports idempotent apply: running terraform apply twice with same inputs makes no changes
Preflight runner executes a set of configurable probes inside the target VPC and fails fast on critical checks
Canary health-runner can be scheduled as a Kubernetes Job and reports a numeric healthscore to CloudWatch/Datadog
Module has automated Terratest coverage with >= 80% pass rate in the staging harness
Docs include a migration path for clusters using the older eks-controlplane module (simple variable mapping and plan preview)
Rollout plan exists to deploy to sandbox, internal infra, and one non-critical customer canary cluster
implementation_notes: Module will be written in Terraform 1.6 syntax using the recommended module structure (variables.tf, outputs.tf, main.tf, versions.tf)
Remote state: S3 backend with DynamoDB lock table; backend config left to callers but example provided in examples/
IAM: create a minimal IAM role for cluster creation and a separate role for the preflight runner to read KMS and SSM parameters
KMS: accept kms_key_arn variable; when unset, create a customer-managed KMS key and expose the alias output
Preflight runner: small Go binary (health-runner) packaged as container; probes implemented as HTTP, PodExec, and node-metadata checks
Health reporting: emit a single metric 'redwood.priv.eks.health_score' with tags env and cluster_id to CloudWatch / Datadog
Upgrade strategy: module provides lifecycle hooks (pre_upgrade_job, canary_scaleup, canary_duration) and an example automation via SSM Run Command or GitHub Actions
Outputs: cluster_name, kubeconfig_secret_arn, kms_alias, health_runner_ecr_image, preflight_job_template_s3_path
decisions: Use S3 + DynamoDB for terraform state locking by default; callers can override backend config
Prefer a small dedicated 'health-runner' container over embedding probes in the control plane to keep surface area small
Implement preflight checks executed from within the VPC (pod) rather than from the control plane to avoid cross-VPC networking issues
Create a lightweight convention for numeric health_score (0-100) where <60 is considered high-risk and blocks automated rollouts

testing_plan: Unit: validate variable schema and plan diffs using tflint and terraform validate in CI
Integration: run Terratest in staging that creates a small EKS cluster using module examples/simple; validate kubeconfig, node registration, and health-runner job execution
Chaos: simulate a failed upgrade by introducing a kernel parameter change in canary nodes and verify health-score drops and rollback hooks trigger
Security: run least-privilege IAM analyzer and key policy checks in CI for autogenerated KMS keys
Performance: measure health-runner overhead and ensure <2s cold-start and <5% CPU on burst checks
rollout_plan: Phase 0: apply module to sandbox account using examples/sandbox and validate acceptance criteria
Phase 1: internal infra deploy to non-prod clusters for two weeks and monitor health_score and metrics
Phase 2: pick one low-risk customer cluster as canary with operator approval — run canary upgrades for minor versions only
Phase 3: general availability behind feature-flag and Gradual opt-in for existing clusters with migration scripts
Rollback: if health_score <60 for >10m during canary, trigger automated rollback job and notify SRE on-call
risks: IAM misconfiguration could allow excessive privileges for health-runner; mitigate via CI IAM analyzer and manual review
KMS rotation edge-cases: verify that created keys are properly aliased and accessible to both provisioner and runtime
State drift: large numbers of manual edits to caller-managed resources could produce unexpected plan changes; document safe patterns
Probe flakiness could block upgrades — include a degraded_mode that allows manual override for emergency patches
